title: 01 · Understand
section: Price is only one part of the decision
text:
Price is only one part of the decision
A larger PV system can generate more electricity, but Cape Manufacturing only saves money on solar electricity it can use when it is produced. This makes self-consumption the bridge between technical output and economic value.
If a system generates 100 kWh while the factory can use only 80 kWh, its self-consumption is 80%. In this simplified case, unused generation has no economic value.

Check your answer

Open Start Here and read the brief. The five tabs keep the work traceable: Start Here provides orientation, Case Data holds inputs, Your Model contains your Year-1 calculations, Test Assumptions supports sensitivity analysis, and Recommendation records your advice.

South African commercial context

Cape Manufacturing is a fictional Western Cape industrial producer. All monetary values are in South African Rand (R). The electricity tariff, escalation rate and other financial parameters are assumptions, not forecasts of South African tariffs or investment conditions. Unless stated otherwise, use the figures exactly as provided and do not introduce VAT, tax, financing or feed-in revenue into the model.

title: Reviewer Rationale
section: One case, one model, one professional decision
text:
One case, one model, one professional decision
This 65–80 minute authentic learning activity integrates Microsoft Excel competence with professional judgement. Students interpret business data, construct an auditable model, test a material assumption, evaluate conflicting investment measures and communicate a qualified recommendation. Formative checkpoints, scaffolding and reflection move the learner from spreadsheet operator to analyst to professional adviser.

title: Reviewer Rationale
section: Constructive alignment
text:
Constructive alignment
The four learner-facing outcomes connect directly to observable work:

Build an auditable model: interpret inputs; enter and copy formulas; apply appropriate references and number formats. Evidence: Your Model!B4:D7, the reference-error checkpoint and optional payback ranks in row 8.
Analyse financial results: compare payback and NPV, create a relevant chart and test C’s self-consumption. Evidence: chart with rationale, Test Assumptions!A7:E14 and crossover interpretation.
Evaluate assumptions and claims: explain operational uncertainty and specify credible evidence before relying on the environmental claim. Evidence: load-profile explanation and Recommendation!A22.
Communicate a recommendation: select a proposal using at least two correctly interpreted results, one trade-off and one operational qualification. Evidence: Recommendation!A7, limited to 100 words.

Reflection extends these outcomes to another investment decision. The detailed skills support foundational competence (understand), practical competence (model and communicate) and reflexive competence (evaluate and transfer).

title: Reviewer Rationale
section: Scaffolding and formative assessment
text:
Scaffolding and formative assessment
The sequence is Start → Understand → Spreadsheet Essentials → Build → Test → Decide → Reflect. Spreadsheet Essentials introduces only the prerequisite moves. Build supplies guided formulas, then asks learners to diagnose a copied-reference error. Test supplies model infrastructure so effort goes into manipulating assumptions and interpreting results, rather than transcribing a long formula.
An initial prediction makes prior judgement explicit. Answer disclosures support self-checking; diagnostic feedback and the reasoning question prompt correction. Decide’s checklist makes success criteria visible. The completed reference workbook is available on Reflect, after the modelling and recommendation tasks.

title: Reviewer Rationale
section: Professional accountancy relevance
text:
Professional accountancy relevance
A has the shortest payback while C has the highest base-case NPV. Neither metric automatically determines the recommendation. The learner must explain a decision rule, test the utilisation assumption and distinguish model evidence from an unverified sustainability claim.
The spreadsheet gives evidence. It does not choose the decision rule.
Microsoft Excel is the primary learning platform. Google Sheets notes provide a compatibility pathway without changing the model. The five-sheet workbook, Rand values and fictional Western Cape case maintain a coherent professional context. Tariff and escalation values are teaching assumptions, not forecasts.
This is a non-credit application demonstration. Its intended alignment is with digital, analytical, communication and professional-judgement capabilities; formal Stellenbosch module or SAICA competency mapping requires the approved outcomes and assessment documentation.

title: 03 · Test
section: Will we really use 78% of System C’s output?
text:
Will we really use 78% of System C’s output?
Production varies during the week. If we cannot use as much solar power at the time it is generated as Supplier C assumes, does C still offer the highest net present value (NPV)?

title: 03 · Test
section: “Will we really use 78% of System C’s output?”
text:
“Will we really use 78% of System C’s output?”
Simple payback favours System A at about 2.92 years. A 20-year discounted cash-flow view tells a different story: under the base assumptions, System C has the highest NPV at about R2.871 million.
Why? Payback focuses on recovery speed. NPV considers the value today of future net savings over the full analysis period.
Hold the assumptions for A and B fixed while varying C’s self-consumption. This isolates the effect of the operational uncertainty.
